claim: Majority vote over 5-40 sampled CoT paths raises accuracy on math and reasoning for capable models; e.g. PaLM-540B GSM8K 56.5 -> 74.4, code-davinci-002 60.1 -> 78.0, More Agents GSM8K +12 to +24 points, and R1-distilled models gain 10 to 30 points on AIME 2024 at cons@64 (Distill-Qwen-14B +10.3 to Distill-Llama-8B +29.6).
agent_test: Equal-token test: 1 long reasoning pass vs k short samples + code-side modal vote, k=5,10,20 on our task set.
audit_note: R1 Table 15: distilled models gain 10.3 to 29.6 points at cons@64 on AIME 2024 (Distill-Llama-8B 50.4 to 80.0 is +29.6), not 10-28; other numbers (56.5 to 74.4; 60.1 to 78.0; More Agents GSM8K 12-24 points) match.
claim_before_audit: Majority vote over 5-40 sampled CoT paths raises accuracy on math and reasoning for capable models; e.g. PaLM-540B GSM8K 56.5 -> 74.4, code-davinci-002 60.1 -> 78.0, More Agents GSM8K +12 to +24 points, R1-distills AIME gain 10-28 pts at cons@64.

claim: Gain from voting grows with base model capability up to a point and is near zero when the model cannot solve the task at all (UL2 Letter 0.0 -> 0.0) or when the base is near ceiling (AddSub +1.8).
agent_test: Bin items by single-sample pass rate; report vote gain per bin.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Most of the vote gain on easy and mid items comes from about 5-10 samples (Wang advice 5-10; USC about 8; no gain past 5 on SummScreen). On hard reasoning-model items gains continue much further: GPT-OSS-120B AIME25 pass@1 91.8 -> cons@512 97.0, DeepSeek-8B HMMT25 58.1 -> 69.6 at 512 samples, and about 80 samples are usually needed for Bo-infinity accuracy. The knee depends on difficulty.
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs k at equal tokens per difficulty bin; default 5 for easy items, allow up to 16-64 for hard items under an adaptive stop.

claim: Adaptive stopping (stop sampling when the top answer leads) cuts samples 2-5x on average (up to 7.9x; 33.8-84.2% fewer in ESC; 2x-5x in Bo-infinity; 58% fewer in CGES; up to 84.7% fewer tokens in DeepConf online) with under 0.1-0.4 pp accuracy loss on average. Savings are smallest on hard items: at budget 16, ESC uses 12.88 calls on GPQA and 10.68 on AIME24 vs 5.16 on GSM8K, and a confidence-guided rule cannot stop early where its signal is uninformative (GPQA lost about 2 pp).
agent_test: Sequential vote with Beta/Dirichlet stopping vs fixed k; measure tokens saved at same accuracy.
audit_note: Slight blending across papers: GPQA ~2 pp loss is ESC -2.0 and CGES-LNS -2.3 (budget 16); '2-5x on average' is a loose summary of Bo-infinity 2x-5x and Adaptive-Consistency 3.3x average.

claim: Answer agreement beats model likelihood as a selector: unnormalised weighted sum 59.9 vs plain vote 74.4 on GSM8K; sample-and-rank gains much smaller than vote gain.
agent_test: Compare plain vote vs likelihood-weighted vote on our model if logprobs available. (Later CISC/Soft-SC show better weights help; see C01.02-K06.)

claim: Confidence-aware aggregation beats plain vote in most author-reported tests: CISC cuts needed samples over 40%; Soft-SC +4.2% avg; DeepConf top-10% filtering lifts DeepSeek-8B HMMT25 from 69.6 to 79.5-83.9 and cuts tokens up to 84.7%; CGES saves 58% of calls. Exceptions: DeepConf on GPT-OSS-120B HMMT25 fell from 92.9 to 90.5/88.9 (over-confident wrong traces), and self-certainty scored at random level (75.83 vs 76.25) in an independent Bo5 AIME-2025 test.
agent_test: Ask agent to rate its own confidence per path (within-question ranking), weight vote; compare at equal samples.
audit_note: All numbers match; but CISC and CGES are efficiency gains at equal accuracy (not accuracy gains over plain vote) and Soft-SC +4.2% is for CodeLlama-34B on agent tasks, so 'beats plain vote' is loose.

claim: In Large Language Monkeys (Brown et al. 2024), coverage keeps rising with sampling while voting and reward-model selection plateau near 100 samples (Llama-3-8B-Instruct MATH: coverage 82.9 to 98.44% from 100 to 10,000 samples; majority vote or reward model 40.50 to 41.41%); in domains with automatic verifiers (tests, proof checkers) coverage translates into accuracy (SWE-bench Lite with DeepSeek-Coder-V2 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples), though the authors note even such verifiers are imperfect. Single-paper evidence.
agent_test: Where a runnable check exists, select by execution/test instead of vote; compare to vote at equal samples.
audit_note: Numbers match Brown et al. 2024, but 'only closed by an automatic verifier' is stronger than the paper (it says coverage turns into accuracy where verifiers exist and warns that even unit-test verifiers are imperfect, Sec 4.2); five of six evidence lines are the same paper, with Cobbe 2021 not bearing on the voting result.
claim_before_audit: Voting plateaus while coverage keeps rising: Llama-3-8B MATH coverage 82.9 -> 98.44% (100 -> 10,000 samples), vote/reward model 40.50 -> 41.41%. The gap is only closed by an automatic verifier (tests, proof checker): SWE-bench Lite 15.9 -> 56% at 250 samples.

claim: Vote can make things worse on hard items: when the correct answer is not the plurality, more samples harden the wrong answer. Chen et al.: MMLU-Physics 53% easy queries improve, 47% hard queries degrade; wrong answer 56% vs correct 34% in their example.
agent_test: Route by agreement level: when top-answer share is low, do not trust the vote, escalate to verifier or search.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Samples from one model share errors in open-ended output (pairwise similarity above 0.8 in 79% of cases for one model) and wrong answers across models agree about 60% vs 1/3 by chance. But for short-answer math at T=1.0, the within-question correlation of correct votes measured in AIMO 3 was already at or below zero (19 of 19 estimates negative), and cross-question structure from one model's independent draws was not detectable unless seeds or few-shot prompts were shared. The real failure is items whose per-sample chance is below 50%, not correlation between samples.
agent_test: Measure our samples' pairwise answer agreement on wrong items; test whether temperature or persona diversity lowers it.

claim: Diversity of prompts helps beyond resampling one prompt in some tests: DiVeRSe 5 prompts x 20 samples 80.0 vs 76.7 (code-davinci-002 GSM8K). But 40 prompt permutations (19.2) lose to 40 sampled paths (27.7) on LaMDA, complexity-voting adds only +0.3 to +1.1, and on gpt-oss-120b (AIMO 3, 50 problems) every prompt-diversity mix scored equal or worse than the baseline (39.3), with temperature already giving the diversity.
agent_test: Compare same-prompt T=1.0 sampling with a prompt-rewrite mix at equal k; do not assume the mix wins.

claim: Plain vote versus verifiers depends on verifier type and budget. Trained or generative verifiers and PRMs beat plain vote at larger N: PRM best-of-1860 78.2 vs majority 69.6; Heimdall 70.0 (majority) to 83.3 on AIME2025; RL^V weighted vote above majority at N>=8; compute-optimal allocation about 4x more efficient than best-of-N. But at N=5 with off-the-shelf judges and reward models on AIME-2025 (GPT-OSS-20B) majority vote 85.42 beat LLM-judge 81.25-82.92 and reward models about 79.8-80.0.
agent_test: Compare vote vs step-level check on a subset where we can verify steps.

claim: Majority voting helps strong reasoning models too, but gains are model-dependent and agreement is a weak trust signal for the most consistent model: R1 AIME 79.8 -> 86.7 at cons@64; GPT-4o 9.3 -> 13.4; Gemini 1.5 Pro consistency@200 only 1 -> 4 of 15 AIME while verification@200 gave 8; gpt-4.1 had C=0.89 vs mini 0.82 with no accuracy advantage.
agent_test: Report pass@1, maj@k and verifier@k on same items with token counts.
audit_note: gpt-4.1 vs mini 'no accuracy advantage' (0.48 each) comes from Ding's own K=20, 48-case re-run; the single-author preprint flags a possible model-snapshot confound.

claim: Universal self-consistency (model picks the most consistent of its own free-form samples) matches answer-extraction SC on math (GSM8K 90.2 vs 90.4 PaLM 2-L) and execution voting on code, enabling vote on free-form output; it saturates at about 5-8 samples and is limited by context length and order/length bias.
agent_test: Use model-as-selector for free-form items; shuffle order 5x to check stability.

claim: Gain is larger for weaker models and harder tasks in relative terms (Llama2-13B 28-200% vs GPT-3.5 8-16%; MATH 34-200% vs GSM8K 16-69%), and Llama2-13B ensemble 59% beat single Llama2-70B 54% on GSM8K.
agent_test: Check whether k small-model samples beat one large-model pass at equal FLOPs.

claim: Voting repairs weak prompts and works zero-shot: LaMDA imperfect prompt 14.9 -> 23.4; PaLM zero-shot CoT 43.0 -> 69.2.
agent_test: Vote over zero-shot CoT as a fallback when no exemplars exist.

claim: Agreement rate is correlated with accuracy (Wang Fig 5), and a threshold on vote share can control confident errors where the score separates right from wrong (Pause and Reflect: 90.1% selective accuracy at under 5% abstention vs 82% on GSM8K, 200 calibration items; TT-SC AUROC 0.836 vs 0.655 for token probabilities). But the link is weak and regime-dependent: Spearman 0.20-0.59 with correctness, and for gpt-4.1 on GPQA, C>=0.8 occurred on 77% of entries and 48% of those were wrong. Not a fixed-threshold trust test; calibrate per model and task.
agent_test: Log vote share vs correctness per model and task; fit a binned table on about 200 labelled items; escalate below the threshold; treat unanimous answers from frontier models as not proven.
audit_note: TT-SC AUROC 0.836 vs 0.655 and Pause-and-Reflect 90.1% at under 5% abstention vs 82% match; 200 calibration items and small open models only.

claim: Debate and other multi-agent schemes are not reliably better than plain self-consistency at matched compute; stacking debate with vote failed for Llama2 code.
agent_test: Plain vote vs debate at equal tokens.

claim: Voting is a weak check when tests are incomplete: on HumanEval/MBPP the best number of attempts is often under 10 because false positives are accepted.
agent_test: Measure false-accept rate of our checks before scaling samples.

claim: Sequential vs parallel at equal tokens is unresolved. Sequential refinement beat parallel vote in 43 of 45 settings with 4096-token chains on 20B-235B models (Qwen3-235B AIME-2025 76.7 vs 30.0), but designed paired tests on 1.5B-7B models found every self-inspection method (critique, refine, reflect, pick-best) worse than repeated sampling at equal tokens (18 of 18 negative). Naive revision turned about 38% of correct answers wrong in Snell. The best mix depends on difficulty, model size and chain-length cap.
agent_test: Parallel vs revise at equal tokens by difficulty bin.

claim: Test-time reinforcement learning uses majority-vote labels as reward (Qwen2.5-Math-7B AIME24 12.9 -> 40.2); outside scaffold-only scope.
agent_test: Not testable without training.

claim: At equal measured tokens, a plain vote over repeated samples is not reliably beaten by Self-Refine, Reflexion, model-picks-best-of-N or other self-inspection methods on small models (1.5B-7B, GSM8K and MATH-500, 36 paired comparisons: 10 reliably worse, none better). The gap for model-picks-best-of-8 shrinks with size (8.0-11.3 points at 1.5B, 1.3-2.0 at 7B, not distinguishable from zero).
agent_test: Run vote-of-k against each fancier operator at equal tokens on our model size; only keep an operator that wins with a paired CI.
audit_note: Mirzaei 2026 is a single small preprint (150 questions per setting, Qwen2.5 only); Wang et al. 2024 supports the direction (budget-matched CoT+SC matches or beats debate/Reflexion) but was read at abstract level only.

claim: No clean study measures k short CoT samples with a vote against one long thinking pass at equal total tokens on frontier models. The closest evidence is thin: the Sequential Edge (parallel chains capped at 4096 tokens lose to sequential refinement), a 30-item AIME24 test on small Qwen3 models, and m1 (medical thinking gains saturate near 4K tokens, voting untested).
agent_test: Measure our own curve: accuracy vs tokens for one pass of length L vs k passes of L/k, by difficulty bin.

claim: Vote share is a usable but fragile stop/escalate signal. It ranks answers well (TT-SC AUROC 0.836, ECE 0.090 over 36 model-dataset combinations) and can be thresholded with conformal risk control from about 200 labelled items, but only if the score separates right from wrong (it did not on HotpotQA), and frontier models can be over-confident (gpt-4.1 GPQA: 48% wrong at C>=0.8).
agent_test: Fit a per-task threshold on about 200 labelled items; test separability first; escalate to verifier/search under the threshold.

claim: For items without a runnable check, the best code-side selector is not settled. Plain vote beat LLM judges (81.25-82.92), reward models (about 79.8-80.0) and self-certainty (75.83) at N=5 on AIME-2025 with GPT-OSS-20B (85.42), but on GAIA agent trajectories a list-wise judge (63.03) beat voting (56.8), and confidence-weighted voting helped in other studies. Choice depends on whether answers can be matched exactly.
agent_test: Use plain vote when answers match exactly; use a list-wise or USC-style call when they are free-form; compare both on our own items.

claim: Prompt, persona and rewrite diversity adds little on top of temperature-1.0 sampling for short-answer math, and sharing a seed or few-shot block across a pass creates false agreement. Cheap levers: separate seed per sample, shuffled option order on multiple choice.
agent_test: Check per-sample seeds are independent and shuffle option letters across samples before voting.

claim: Vote selection loss, not missing coverage, is the main remaining gap on hard math: gpt-oss-120b best vote 42/50 vs pass@20 45.5; majority vote is the worst scaling rule at equal N once a trained verifier exists (Heimdall: majority about 70% vs 83.3%), and voting is trapped when a wrong answer is the mode. A verifier on the top few distinct answers is the natural hybrid.
agent_test: Run a verifier or check only on the top 2-3 distinct answers when vote share is below the calibrated threshold.
audit_note: Minor: majority 70% vs 83.3% is a 32B-solver AIME2025 result, a different setting from gpt-oss-120b; 'wrong answer is the mode' is the authors' framing, not a measured number.

claim: On non-math science sets the vote gain is smaller and early stopping saves less: GPQA-Diamond cons@512 vs pass@1 +9.7 (DeepSeek-8B) and +3.3 (Qwen3-32B) vs +11.5 on HMMT25; ESC saves 3.1 of 16 calls on GPQA vs 10.8 on GSM8K. No held-out vote study on law, biology or causal tasks was found; medical thinking-budget gains saturate near 4K tokens.
agent_test: Do not extrapolate AIME gains to knowledge-limited tasks; measure on a held-out set of our own with at least 100 items.

claim: For agent and free-form tasks, counting answers is a weak selector: GAIA best-of-4 merging gave voting 56.8, scoring 59.39, list-wise 63.03 (baseline 55.76, 165 tasks). Naive reflection lowered the score (55.15).
agent_test: For open tasks let a judge see all candidates together, with plain vote only on matchable fields.
